LATEST SIGHTINGS

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A truly South African Social Media Success Story – a concepts that’s boosting tourism and making big bucks.

Summary:

Latest¬ Sightings is one of the most watched South African YouTube Channels in the world with 310+ million total views!

The videos are seen all around the world, with the US, Brazil, India and South Korea – a teenager’s clever concept has turned into a great showcase for SA tourism!

The concept even generates cash for the contributors – making them anything from a couple of hundred rands to hundreds of thousands!

This is the story of a young man’s passion for wildlife that’s turned into a global social media phenomenon.



Further information:
HOW IT GOT STARTED
Latestsightings.com was started by teenager Nadav Ossendryver who is Kruger Park and animal mad. When in the park he would constantly be asking his parents to stop to ask people what animals they'd seen. He then realised that he could make an app where people could share what they'd seen so many people could enjoy more animal sightings. He borrowed a friend's MacBook over school holidays, taught himself to program and emerged at the end of the school holidays with an app, some whatsapp groups, social media pages and a website where people could share their sightings. He would then update and manage the various platforms during school break.

TURNING A HOBBY INTO A BUSINESS
People started sharing interesting videos and he set up a YouTube Channel. Averages about 400 000 views daily, generating worldwide interest in South Africa and it’s wildlife.

2 years ago he formalised things and started a company called Latest Sightings Pty Ltd (latestsightings.com). He started a "film and earn" programme where people who had caught exciting footage could share in the income earned. Some people make a few cents a month, and some people really do well. Contributor’s range from game rangers, to school teachers and even retired wildlife fans.

THERE’s METHOD BEHIND THE MAGIC
The videos don’t just magically go viral, Nadav and the team have become quite expert at analyzing what footage can do well and putting in place the right strategies for that certain video. They look at the type of video it is, together with the audience it can reach and finally, seeing if it can link to current events. Then once they have the strategy in place, they send the video to their media contacts around the world to then publish the video for thousands, and sometimes millions, of people.

Four great case studies:

Baby Elephant calf vs birds

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kIy5aiRdtrc

This was sent in by a lecturer and researcher at Wits. It went viral and the virality lasted about 2 months. She made around R50 000 which she used to finance elephant research and a small bursary.

Lion Shows Tourist why you must stay in your car

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JRSYMfC2PFU

This is the most viewed video on the channel and is one of the most watched SA wildlife clips in the world with 81,5 million views. It was submitted by Mr Gert de Koker, a retiree from Kempton Park. He has made close on R200 000 from the video over the last 2 years and continues to earn a few thousand rand every month depending on how it does for the month.

2 leopards vs 1 huge python

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TA-NALgEw9s

This was sent in by a guide. He's made around R10 000 in total from this video and continues to earn a few hundred rand per month.

Battle Between Leopard & Wildebeest Mother over Calf | Graphic

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Gxaf0Kqen8c

This was sent in by a 12 year old, and he is too, earning a few thousand every month from it so far.

Press Release:


Viral Wildlife - Latest Sightings
It’s one of the most watched South African YouTube Channels and it’s given a clever teenager a thriving online business. Carte Blanche reports on a home-grown app that brings the elusive world of South African wildlife viewing to the world.


Script:


STRUCTURE

VO: What started off as a passion for wildlife has morphed into a global social media phenomenon.

Today, the Latest Sightings Youtube channel is one of the most watched in South Africa - with 318 million views globally!

NADAV: To think that on average we get 5 views every second - that’s five people around the world

VO: 19 year old Nadav Ossendryver is the young man behind this clever mobile app that shares locations of animal sightings in game reserves. He’s just been listed as the youngest African Entrepreneur on Forbes’ Top 30 under 30!

He was just 15 years old when he came up with the concept on a game reserve trip – when he wasn’t having much luck with animal sightings.

NADAV: So I felt like if there was a community sharing sightings // maybe I could go there and see it and other people could do it as same

VO: The app evolved into a YouTube channel for wildlife sightings.

Social Media Expert Candice de Carvalho says it works, Latest Sightings is built on marketing strategies fuelled by crowdsourcing.

CANDICE: it’s fairly easy to monetise your content within youtube, but it’s not a get rich quick scheme. // It doesn’t necessarily get views by itself

VO: Retiree, Gert de Koker is one of 200 contributors. While Gert’s video was not that exciting, it is the channel’s biggest video ever! - with 81 million views!

GERT: I saw this car of the two little kiddies hanging out of the window trying to take videos out of the car’s window.

VO: The clip shows the potential danger of getting too close to the wild side – watch as the lions roars at the kids in the car.

LINK: Social Media isn’t an exact science – there’s no telling what is going to go viral, sometimes you’re lucky but most of the time it’s because there is a cleverly crafted campaign.

NADAV: There is a lot that actually goes into making a video go viral. The thumbnail is so important – the first thing you do when you type something in youtube, you look at the thumbnail before you even read the title.

VO: Realising the channel had earning potential through an advertising partnership with YouTube – Nadav decided to formalise an agreement with contributors.

NADAV: The videos aren’t mine, it’s shared by the community, we want to reward them for loving wildlife and filming this amazing sighting.

VO: Gert’s 81 million views earned him close to R180 000.

While Nadav is not obliged to split the YouTube earnings – he has entered into 60 /40 revenue share with the contributors. Keeping 60% for operational costs like editing and marketing – a recipe that is working!

Contributors are from all walks of life – making money off their holidays.

This clip is from Khimbini Hlongwane, a Game Ranger submits clips often - this one earned him R13 000.

Susan Webb, a Geology Professor. Her EARNINGS: R55 000. The money funds an elephant research bursary.

Part of Nadav’s success is that he has built social media communities around a general shared interest - a love for safari.

CANDICE: They’ve tapped into very highly valued, quality content // that are rare sightings that would take a Discovery Channel Team months and months to find.

BONGANI: What makes a good clip?
NADAV: it has to be authentic. When people go to the game reserve – there are people screaming – look at that lion – you get really excited – in narrated videos you don’t feel that. And the biggest thing that causes people to share videos is when they connect to it.

UPSOUND VIDEO – screaming.

VO: And then there are more graphic clips, like this one from 12 year old Muhammad Sa’ad Gardee. He’s earned close to R5000 from over a million views.

BONGANI: were you scared?
MUHAMMAD: I was more excited – ad the adrenalin was just pumping – so I didn’t have any emotion at the time. INT2 M2
BONGANI: Did you feel sorry for the Wildebeest?
MUHAMMAD: Just a little bit, but I was more happy for the leopard. // that’s nature. INT2 M3

VO: Most contributors use the app to find wild life. Sharing sightings is pretty straight forward – You Log on, enter some basic info - the location, the time and then of course which animals you’ve seen– you can even add a photographs.

NADAV: The best thing is even if you don’t signal it will find you location to accuracy around 30 meters – after a while it will go down to around 5 meters. //you can add a comment… wow – to create an atmosphere.. INT2 M4

VO: While wildlife is far removed from technology, apps like this are linking it together – a trend not welcomed by all.

SANPARKS Reynold Thakhuli says they are concerned about tourist losing sight of safety regulations when it comes to chasing animal sightings.

REYNOLD: The minute our customers get these alerts on these mobile alerts they rush to the scene and in most instances there seems to be road rages ensue.

VO: He says there will be consequences for reckless and lawless behaviour.

REYNOLD: We want to emphasise that those that are found speeding will be arrested and we will evoke penalties – fines and those can range anything from 3000 to 10 000 rand.

VO: SANPARKS appeals to wild life lovers to be more conscious at sightings. Nadav says they do try to be responsible with their app – and even have a feature to highlight traffic to avoid pile-ups.

He believes Latest Sightings does more good than harm.

NADAV: We’re not just helping people see animals, we’re helping them fall in love with nature as well, you know creating a passion in wildlife. INT1 M8

PROMOS

10 SECOND PROMO
VO: One of the most watched South African YouTube Channels is bringing African wildlife to world with videos.

NADAV: the biggest thing that causes people to share videos is when they connect to it.

15 SECOND PROMO
VO: A home-grown mobile app brings the elusive world of wildlife viewing to the world.

NADAV: We’re not just helping people see animals, we’re helping them fall in love with nature as well, you know creating a passion in wildlife.

15 SECOND PROMO
VO: Crowdsourcing is the secret behind a young South African’s booming social media business – turning a passion into profit.

NADAV: The videos aren’t mine, it’s shared by the community, we want to reward them for loving wildlife and filming this amazing sighting.
